name: Duomo Florence
cardImageAlt: Duomo Florence Santa Maria del Fiore Cathedral and Dome
cardTagline: Climb Brunelleschi's iconic dome and explore Florence's monumental Gothic cathedral.
heroHeading: Duomo Florence Tickets & Brunelleschi Dome Climb
heroSubheading: Experience Santa Maria del Fiore, one of the world's most breathtaking architectural achievements. Ascend the 463 steps of Brunelleschi's Dome for panoramic views across Florence and Tuscany.
heroImageAlt: Florence Cathedral Brunelleschi's Dome bathed in sunlight
highlightsHeading: Types of Duomo Florence Tickets & Passes
highlightsSubheading: The Cathedral complex offers specialized passes and guided climb options covering all 5 monumental areas.

highlights.title: Brunelleschi Pass
highlights.body: All-access pass: Dome Climb (463 steps), Giotto's Bell Tower, Baptistery of San Giovanni, Opera del Duomo Museum, and Santa Reparata Crypt.

highlights.title: Giotto Pass
highlights.body: Includes Giotto's Campanile (414 steps), Baptistery, Museum, and Crypt — ideal if you want panoramic views without the Dome climb.

highlights.title: Ghiberti Pass
highlights.body: Explores the ground monuments: Baptistery, Opera del Duomo Museum, and ancient Santa Reparata crypt ruins.

highlights.title: Guided Dome Tour
highlights.body: Fast-track skip-the-line entrance with an expert art historian guide, including exclusive access and historical commentary.

aboutHeading: Things to Do at Duomo Florence
aboutBody: The Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore stands as the crown jewel of Florence. Climb 463 steps to reach the highest point in central Florence atop Brunelleschi's revolutionary double-shell dome; gaze upward at Giorgio Vasari and Federico Zuccari's monumental fresco of The Last Judgment; marvel at Lorenzo Ghiberti's gilded bronze Gates of Paradise at the Baptistery; and admire Michelangelo's unfinished Bandini Pietà in the state-of-the-art Opera del Duomo Museum.
toursHeading: Duomo Florence Tickets & Guided Dome Climb Tours

practicalGettingThere: Located in the heart of historic Florence. An easy 8-minute walk from Firenze Santa Maria Novella (SMN) railway station.
practicalBestTimeBody: Brunelleschi Pass prices start from €30 for standard access up to €49 for guided fast-track tours. Modest dress code is strictly enforced: shoulders and knees must remain covered to enter the cathedral and religious sites.

name: Uffizi Gallery
cardImageAlt: Uffizi Gallery Florence grand renaissance corridor
cardTagline: See Botticelli's Birth of Venus, Michelangelo and Renaissance masterpieces in one of the world's greatest art museums.
heroSubheading: Discover the birthplace of the Italian Renaissance. The Uffizi Gallery houses the world's most priceless collection of Renaissance masterpieces by Botticelli, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael.
highlightsSubheading: Explore iconic paintings and classical Roman sculptures collected by the Medici family.

highlights.title: The Birth of Venus
highlights.body: Sandro Botticelli's legendary tempera masterpiece depicting the goddess Venus emerging from the sea foam.

highlights.title: Botticelli's Primavera
highlights.body: An enchanting allegorical depiction of Spring featuring Flora, Mercury, and the Three Graces in an orange grove.

highlights.title: Leonardo da Vinci Room
highlights.body: Home to Da Vinci's masterworks including the Annunciation and the mesmerizing Adoration of the Magi.

highlights.title: The Tribune & Grand Corridors
highlights.body: The octagonal Tribune encrusted with mother-of-pearl and corridors framed by Roman marble statuary.

aboutHeading: Things to Do at Uffizi Gallery
aboutBody: The Uffizi Gallery, designed by Giorgio Vasari in 1560 for Grand Duke Cosimo I de' Medici, is a temple of fine arts. Admire Caravaggio's dramatic Medusa, Michelangelo's Doni Tondo, Titian's Venus of Urbino, and Raphael's Madonna of the Goldfinch. Enjoy sweeping views of Ponte Vecchio and the Arno River from the second-floor windows, then stop by the rooftop terrace café overlooking Piazza della Signoria.
toursSubheading: Choose timed priority admission, small-group guided tours, or Uffizi + Accademia combination passes.
practicalHoursNote: Closed every Monday. Booking timed skip-the-line tickets in advance is strictly required to avoid 2-3 hour queues.
practicalAddress: Piazzale degli Uffizi 6, 50122 Firenze FI, Italy.
practicalGettingThere: Located adjacent to Piazza della Signoria and Palazzo Vecchio. A quick 5-minute walk from the Duomo and 12 minutes from SMN station.
practicalBestTimeBody: Priority timed entry tickets start at €26. Free admission is granted to EU youth under 18 with valid government ID. Early morning (8:15 AM) and late afternoon (after 3:30 PM) offer the most peaceful atmosphere.
priceSubheading: Compare skip-the-line tickets and small-group guided experiences.
priceNote: All tickets include full access to permanent collections and temporary exhibitions.

name: Accademia Gallery
cardImageAlt: Michelangelo David statue in Galleria dell'Accademia Florence
cardTagline: Stand in front of Michelangelo's David and discover Florence's artistic heritage.
heroSubheading: Marvel at the pinnacle of Renaissance sculpture. Stand beneath the skylight of the Tribune and behold Michelangelo's world-famous marble statue of David in all its majestic detail.
highlightsSubheading: Discover Michelangelo's greatest sculptures and precious Renaissance instruments.

highlights.title: Michelangelo's David
highlights.body: Carved from a single block of Carrara marble between 1501 and 1504, standing over 5 meters tall.

highlights.title: Hall of the Prisoners (Slaves)
highlights.body: Four unfinished marble statues demonstrating Michelangelo's non-finito technique of liberating figures from stone.

highlights.title: Museum of Musical Instruments
highlights.body: The Medici and Lorraine court collection including the world's oldest surviving Stradivari violin.

highlights.title: Gothic & Renaissance Paintings
highlights.body: Extensive gold-ground altarpieces by Giotto, Orcagna, Botticelli, and Domenico Ghirlandaio.

aboutHeading: Things to Do at Accademia Gallery
aboutBody: Galleria dell'Accademia was founded in 1784 by Grand Duke Peter Leopold of Lorraine as a teaching facility for students of the Academy of Fine Arts. The undisputed centerpiece is Michelangelo's David, moved here from Piazza della Signoria in 1873 to protect it from weather damage. Walk through the Hall of the Colossus, examine Giambologna's plaster model for the Rape of the Sabine Women, and admire the collection of historical musical instruments.
toursHeading: Accademia Gallery Tickets & Guided Highlights Tours
toursSubheading: Secure fast-track timed entrance or join an art historian for an inspiring tour of David.
practicalHoursNote: Closed Mondays. Advance reservation is mandatory to guarantee entry.
practicalGettingThere: Situated between Piazza San Marco and Piazza del Duomo, a brief 5-minute stroll north from Florence Cathedral.
practicalBestTimeBody: Timed priority tickets start from €20. Combo tickets with the Uffizi Gallery provide a discounted rate for Florence's two premier museums.

name: Ponte Vecchio
cardImageAlt: Ponte Vecchio bridge over Arno river in Florence
cardTagline: Historic medieval stone closed-spandrel arch bridge lined with artisan jewelry shops.
heroSubheading: Florence's most romantic landmark. Built in 1345, the historic Ponte Vecchio is renowned for its charming goldsmith shops and the elevated Vasari Corridor connecting Palazzo Vecchio to Pitti Palace.
highlightsSubheading: Discover the medieval bridge that survived World War II and the Great Flood of 1966.

highlights.title: Goldsmiths & Jewelers
highlights.body: Since Grand Duke Ferdinand I banished butchers in 1593, only goldsmiths and jewelers have traded on the bridge.

highlights.title: Vasari Corridor
highlights.body: The secret enclosed walkway built above the shops so the Medici rulers could walk undisturbed.

highlights.title: Sunset over the Arno
highlights.body: The central viewing arcade offers the most photographed sunset panoramas in Florence.

highlights.title: Benvenuto Cellini Monument
highlights.body: Bronze bust honoring Florence's most celebrated 16th-century master goldsmith.

aboutBody: Ponte Vecchio ('Old Bridge') is the oldest stone bridge in Europe of its kind. As the only bridge in Florence spared from destruction by retreating German forces during WWII, it remains an eternal testament to Florence's resilient heritage. Take an Arno river cruise to view its arches from the water, or join a walking tour through the Oltrarno district.
toursHeading: Ponte Vecchio & Arno River Walking Tours
toursSubheading: Experience guided walking tours, Arno riverboat cruises, and sunset photography tours.
practicalHoursNote: Pedestrian only. Free to walk across at any hour of day or night.
practicalGettingThere: Spans the Arno river connecting Piazza del Duomo / Uffizi to the bohemian Oltrarno quarter.
practicalBestTimeBody: Visit early morning for quiet walks before crowds arrive, or at golden hour sunset when the pastel facades glow over the water.
priceSubheading: Guided walking tours including Ponte Vecchio and Oltrarno.

name: Palazzo Vecchio
cardImageAlt: Palazzo Vecchio and Piazza della Signoria in Florence
cardTagline: Florence's medieval town hall fortress, Salone dei Cinquecento, and the 95m Arnolfo Tower.
heroSubheading: Step inside Florence's imposing fortress-palace. Gaze upon the magnificent Salone dei Cinquecento decorated by Vasari and climb the 95-meter Arnolfo Tower for unmatched views of the Duomo.
heroImageAlt: Palazzo Vecchio tower in Piazza della Signoria
highlightsSubheading: Explore the seat of civic power of the Florentine Republic and Medici Grand Dukes.

highlights.title: Salone dei Cinquecento
highlights.body: The cavernous Hall of the Five Hundred featuring monumental battle frescoes and Michelangelo's Genius of Victory.

highlights.title: Arnolfo Tower Climb
highlights.body: Ascend 223 steps up the medieval crenellated tower for a direct eye-level perspective of Brunelleschi's Dome.

highlights.title: Secret Passages Tour
highlights.body: Guided access through hidden staircases, the Duke of Athens' staircase, and the trussed ceiling above the Salone.

highlights.title: Medici Monumental Apartments
highlights.body: Lavish private chambers of Eleonora di Toledo and Cosimo I decorated with exquisite Renaissance frescoes.

aboutBody: Overlooking Piazza della Signoria, Palazzo Vecchio has served as the political nerve center of Florence since 1299. Today it functions as both the city hall and an extraordinary public museum. Marvel at Donatello's bronze Judith and Holofernes, explore the Hall of Geographical Maps with its massive terrestrial globe, and walk the fortress battlements.
toursHeading: Palazzo Vecchio Museum & Tower Climb Tickets
toursSubheading: Book skip-the-line entrance to the museum, Arnolfo tower climb, and Secret Passages guided tours.
practicalHoursNote: Tower entry is suspended during rain or adverse weather conditions.
practicalAddress: Piazza della Signoria, 50122 Firenze FI, Italy.
practicalGettingThere: Situated on Piazza della Signoria, midway between the Duomo and the Arno River.
practicalBestTimeBody: Museum only tickets start at €12.50; combined Museum + Tower tickets start around €17.50.

name: Boboli Gardens
cardImageAlt: Boboli Gardens fountains and statues in Florence
cardTagline: Grand Renaissance open-air museum, monumental grottos, fountains, and lush pathways.
heroSubheading: Immerse yourself in 45,000 square meters of Renaissance landscape architecture. Created for the Medici dynasty, Boboli Gardens is an outdoor museum adorned with Roman antiquities, grand amphitheaters, and mystical grottos.
heroImageAlt: Boboli Gardens Florence green landscape and statues
highlightsHeading: Top Sights in the Boboli Gardens
highlightsSubheading: Wander through centuries of Italian garden design behind the grand Pitti Palace.

highlights.title: Neptune Fountain & Ocean Basin
highlights.body: Monumental sculptural fountain complex set in the upper reflecting pool.

highlights.title: Buontalenti Grotto
highlights.body: An extravagant Mannerist cave filled with stalactites, frescoed ceilings, and Giambologna's Bathing Venus.

highlights.title: Viottolone Cypress Avenue
highlights.body: A towering cypress avenue lined with classical Roman statues leading down to the Isolotto island.

highlights.title: Kaffeehaus & Porcelain Museum
highlights.body: An 18th-century Rococo pavilion offering panoramic views of the Tuscan hills surrounding Florence.

aboutBody: Directly behind Palazzo Pitti, the Boboli Gardens set the prototype for European royal gardens, directly inspiring Versailles. Walk up to the Knight's Garden for sweeping views over the Tuscan countryside, marvel at the ancient Egyptian obelisk in the central amphitheater, and pair your stroll with a visit to the Palatine Gallery inside Pitti Palace.
toursHeading: Boboli Gardens, Pitti Palace & Bardini Combo Tickets
toursSubheading: Book fast-track timed tickets or comprehensive Medici palace garden tours.

practicalAddress: Piazza de' Pitti 1, 50125 Firenze FI, Italy.
practicalGettingThere: Located on the south bank of the Arno River in the Oltrarno district, a 7-minute walk across Ponte Vecchio.
practicalBestTimeBody: Standard tickets start from €10 in low season and €15 in high season. Comfortable walking shoes are essential as the gardens feature steep terraced slopes.
